mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met over a 5-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of >15% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month * 0.85 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes over the past 20 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4%, signals a supply-side expansion that boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase below 50,000 persons for two consecutive months, despite an unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, indicates labor market softening that depresses consumer spending and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 50000 for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months over the last 15 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment, which often coincides with central bank easing and lower risk-free rates, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above median market returns during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 1.5% while industrial production (INDPRO) grows less than 0.2% signals a consumption-led demand shock that boosts retail sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month * 1.015 AND INDPRO < previous month * 1.002 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) spike above 6.5% in a single month, regardless of other macro conditions, acts as a persistent negative signal for S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to heightened recession risk and consumer confidence collapse.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months over the last 40 years.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1.0% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously rises by at least 0.3 percentage points signals a synchronized supply and labor shock, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month * 0.99 AND UNRATE > previous month + 0.3 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).
